new_mathematical_result: For actual B=C[w,y,t,z]=A[u], E locally nilpotent with Eu=1 and A=ker E, an invariant I=wz-g(y,t) with E^2w=0 and Ew nonzero forces g to be a plane coordinate. There is no degree bound on g or on Ey,Et,Ez. Consequently I is an ambient coordinate and BGL Theorem3.5 recognizes A=C^[3].
proof_chain: A generic smooth fiber Xlambda of I is an affine-surface cylinder Ylambda x C, so H3(Xlambda;Q)=0 by the classical affine homotopy-dimension bound.
The complement w!=0 is C* x C^2. Ordinary tubular excision and relative Kunneth along the trivially normal divisor w=0 give H3(Xlambda;Q)=H1(g=-lambda;Q).

Every smooth generic plane component is A1. Rectify one by Abhyankar-Moh-Suzuki; units on every disjoint component force infinitely many parallel coordinate lines and hence g=P(h) for a plane coordinate h.
Evaluate the finite flow at rational time -w/Ew. The resulting r in Frac B satisfies I=-P(r), so normality puts r in B. If deg P>1, factoring P(r)+lambda contradicts irreducibility of wz-g-lambda.
An explicit plane inverse completes I to actual ambient coordinates; regularity of A and the published regular-kernel theorem give A=C^[3].
application: Both exact derivative corrections of a supplied mixed cubic relation imply coordinate recognition automatically. Primitivity ensures uniqueness but is not required for this implication; the retained intrinsic-plane theorem is likewise not required for the automatic coordinate step.
